title_en: Notice of the General Office of the Supreme People's Court on the Entry into Force of the Treaty between the People's Republic of China and the Republic of the Philippines on Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters
full_text_en:
General Office of the Supreme People's Court

Notice on the Entry into Force of the Treaty between the People's Republic of China and the Republic of the Philippines on Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters

Fa Ban [2012] No. 443

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government:

The Treaty between the People's Republic of China and the Republic of the Philippines on Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters shall enter into force on November 17, 2012. Please handle cases of mutual legal assistance in criminal matters between China and the Philippines in accordance with the provisions of the said Treaty.

Attachment: Treaty between the People's Republic of China and the Republic of the Philippines on Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters

November 6, 2012

Treaty between the People's Republic of China and the Republic of the Philippines on Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters

The People's Republic of China and the Republic of the Philippines (hereinafter referred to as "the Parties"), on the basis of mutual respect for national sovereignty and equality and mutual benefit, and with a view to promoting effective cooperation between the two countries in the field of mutual legal assistance in criminal matters, have agreed as follows:

Article 1 Scope of Assistance

1. The Parties shall, in accordance with the provisions of this Treaty, provide mutual assistance in the investigation, prosecution, and other criminal proceedings in relation to criminal offenses.

2. Assistance shall include:

(a) service of documents;

(b) identifying or locating persons;

(c) obtaining evidence, articles, or documents;

(d) obtaining testimony or statements of persons;

(e) executing requests for search and seizure;

(f) facilitating the testimony of persons;

(g) temporarily transferring persons in custody for the purpose of testifying;

(h) obtaining originals or certified copies of judicial or official records;

(i) tracing, restraining, recovering, and confiscating the proceeds and instrumentalities of criminal activities, including restricting the disposal of or freezing property alleged to be related to criminal matters;

(j) providing and exchanging legal materials, documents, and records;

(k) lending exhibits;

(l) obtaining and providing expert conclusions;

(m) conducting judicial inspections or examinations of sites or articles;

(n) notifying the results of criminal proceedings and providing criminal records;

(o) other forms of assistance consistent with the purposes of this Treaty and not contrary to the law of the Requested Party.

3. This Treaty shall not apply to:

(a) the extradition of persons;

(b) the enforcement of criminal judgments, rulings, or decisions made by the Requesting Party, except as permitted by the law of the Requested Party and this Treaty.

4. This Treaty applies only to the mutual provision of assistance between the Parties. The provisions of this Treaty shall not give rise to a right on the part of any private person to obtain, conceal, or exclude any evidence or to impede the execution of a request.

Article 2 Central Authorities

1. For the purposes of this Treaty, the central authorities designated by each Party shall communicate directly with each other.

2. On the part of the People's Republic of China, the central authority shall be the Ministry of Justice. On the part of the Republic of the Philippines, the central authority shall be the Ministry of Justice.

3. Any change in the designation of the central authority by either Party shall be notified to the other Party through diplomatic channels.

Article 3 Refusal or Postponement of Assistance

1. Assistance may be refused by the Requested Party in any of the following circumstances:

(a) the request relates to conduct that does not constitute an offense under the law of the Requested Party;

(b) the Requested Party considers the request to have been made in respect of a political offense;

(c) the offense to which the request relates is purely a military offense;

(d) the Requested Party has substantial grounds to believe that the request is made for the purpose of investigating, prosecuting, punishing, or otherwise proceeding against a person on account of that person's race, sex, religion, nationality, or political opinion, or that that person's status may be prejudiced for any of these reasons;

(e) the Requested Party is conducting criminal proceedings against the same suspect or defendant in respect of the same offense, or has terminated such proceedings, or has rendered a final judgment;

(f) the Requested Party considers that the assistance requested lacks substantial connection with the case;

(g) the Requested Party considers that execution of the request would prejudice its sovereignty, security, public order, or other essential public interests, or would be contrary to the fundamental principles of its law;

(h) the request for assistance relates to the prosecution of a person and, had the relevant offense been committed within the jurisdiction of the Requested Party, that person could no longer be prosecuted by reason of lapse of time or any other cause;

(i) the Requesting Party cannot comply with any conditions regarding confidentiality or limitation on the use of the materials provided;

(j) the provision of the requested assistance would endanger the safety of any person, or impose an excessive burden on the resources of the Requested Party.

2. The Requested Party may postpone the provision of assistance if such provision would interfere with an ongoing investigation, prosecution, or other proceeding in the Requested Party.

3. Before refusing or postponing assistance, the Requested Party shall consider whether assistance may be granted subject to such conditions as it deems necessary. If the Requesting Party accepts assistance subject to conditions, it shall comply with those conditions.

4. If the Requested Party refuses or postpones assistance, it shall notify the Requesting Party of the reasons for such refusal or postponement.

Article 4 Form and Content of Requests

1. Requests shall be made in writing and signed or sealed by the central authority of the Requesting Party. In urgent circumstances, the Requested Party may accept requests in other forms, and the Requesting Party shall promptly thereafter confirm the request in writing.

2. A request shall include the following:

(a) the name of the competent authority conducting the investigation, prosecution, or other proceedings to which the request relates;

(b) a description of the nature and facts of the case to which the request relates and a statement of the applicable legal provisions;

(c) a description of the assistance requested and its purpose, including an explanation of the relevance of the requested assistance to the case;

(d) the time limit within which the request is desired to be executed.

3. To the extent necessary and possible, a request shall also include the following:

(a) information on the identity and whereabouts of the person to be summoned;

(b) information on the identity and whereabouts of the person to be served, and that person's relationship to the proceedings;

(c) information on the identity and location of the person to be located or identified;

(d) a description of the place or item to be inspected or examined;

(e) a description of the special procedures to be followed in executing the request and the reasons therefor;

(f) a description of the place to be searched and the property to be queried, frozen, or seized;

(g) a statement of the need for confidentiality and the reasons therefor;

(h) a statement of the allowances and expenses to which persons invited to testify or assist in investigations in the territory of the Requesting Party are entitled;

(i) any other information that may assist in the execution of the request.

4. If the Requested Party considers that the content of the request is insufficient to enable it to process the request, it may request additional information.

5. Requests and supporting documents submitted under this Article shall be accompanied by a translation into the language of the Requested Party. However, upon request, such requests and supporting documents may also be in the English language.

Article 5 Execution of Requests

1. Requests for assistance shall be executed promptly in accordance with the law of the Requested Party and, to the extent not prohibited by the law of the Requested Party, in the manner specified in the request, to the extent practicable.

2. The Requested Party shall promptly notify the Requesting Party of the outcome of the execution of the request. If the requested assistance cannot be provided, the Requested Party shall notify the Requesting Party of the reasons.

Article 6 Confidentiality and Limitation on Use

1. Upon request by the Requesting Party, the Requested Party shall keep confidential the request, including its contents and supporting documents, and any action taken pursuant to the request. If the request cannot be executed without breaching confidentiality, the Requested Party shall so inform the Requesting Party, which shall then decide whether the request shall nonetheless be executed.

2. Upon request by the Requested Party, the Requesting Party shall keep confidential the materials and evidence provided by the Requested Party, or shall use them only under the conditions specified by the Requested Party.

3. Without the prior written consent of the Requested Party, the Requesting Party shall not use any materials or evidence obtained under this Treaty for purposes other than the case specified in the request.

Article 7 Service of Documents

1. The Requested Party shall, in accordance with its law and upon request, serve documents transmitted by the Requesting Party. However, the Requested Party shall not be obliged to serve documents requiring the appearance of a person as a defendant.

2. After execution of service, the Requested Party shall provide the Requesting Party with a proof of service. The proof of service shall indicate the date, place, and method of service and shall be signed or sealed by the authority that executed the service. If service cannot be executed, the Requesting Party shall be notified and the reasons given.

Article 8 Obtaining Evidence

1. The Requested Party shall, in accordance with its law and upon request, obtain evidence and transmit it to the Requesting Party.

2. If the request relates to the transmission of documents or records, the Requested Party may transmit certified copies or photocopies. Where the Requesting Party expressly requests originals, the Requested Party shall endeavor to comply with such request to the extent possible.

3. Without prejudice to the law of the Requested Party, documents and other materials transmitted to the Requesting Party under this Article shall be certified in the form requested by the Requesting Party, so as to be admissible under the law of the Requesting Party.

4. Without prejudice to its own law, the Requested Party shall permit persons specified in the request to be present during the execution of the request and shall allow such persons to question, through the judicial personnel of the Requested Party, persons from whom evidence is taken. For this purpose, the Requested Party shall promptly notify the Requesting Party of the time and place of execution of the request.

Article 9 Refusal to Give Evidence

1. A person required to give evidence under this Treaty may refuse to give evidence if the law of the Requested Party permits that person to refuse to give evidence in similar circumstances in proceedings instituted in the Requested Party.

2. If a person required to give evidence under this Treaty claims a right or privilege to refuse to give evidence under the law of the Requesting Party, the Requested Party shall request the Requesting Party to provide a certificate as to the legal basis for such right or privilege. The certificate of the Requesting Party shall be regarded as sufficient evidence of the existence of such right or privilege, unless there is clear evidence to the contrary.

Article 10 Arranging for Persons to Testify or Assist in Investigations

1. Upon request by the Requesting Party, the Requested Party shall invite a person to appear before a competent authority in the territory of the Requesting Party to testify or assist in an investigation. The Requesting Party shall indicate the scope of allowances and expenses to be paid to such person. The Requested Party shall promptly inform the Requesting Party of the person's response.

2. A request for service of documents inviting a person to appear in the territory of the Requesting Party shall be submitted to the Requested Party no later than sixty days before the scheduled date of appearance, unless the Requested Party has agreed, in urgent circumstances, to transmit the documents within a shorter period.

Article 11 Transfer of Persons in Custody for the Purpose of Testifying or Assisting Investigations

1. Upon request by the Requesting Party, the Requested Party may temporarily transfer a person in custody in its territory to the territory of the Requesting Party for the purpose of testifying or assisting in an investigation, provided that the person consents and that the Parties have previously reached a written agreement on the conditions of transfer.

2. If, under the law of the Requested Party, the transferred person is required to be held in custody, the Requesting Party shall hold that person in custody.

3. After the person has testified or assisted in the investigation, the Requesting Party shall promptly return the person to the Requested Party.

4. For the purposes of this Article, the period during which the transferred person is held in custody in the Requesting Party shall be deducted from the sentence imposed by the Requested Party.

Article 12 Protection of Witnesses and Experts

1. A witness or expert who appears in the territory of the Requesting Party shall not be investigated, prosecuted, detained, punished, or subjected to any other restriction of personal liberty in the Requesting Party by reason of any act or omission that occurred prior to his or her entry into the territory of the Requesting Party, nor shall that person be required to testify or assist in any investigation, prosecution, or other proceeding other than that to which the request relates, unless the prior consent of the Requested Party and the person has been obtained.

2. Paragraph 1 of this Article shall cease to apply if such person, having been formally notified that his or her presence is no longer required, has not left the territory of the Requesting Party within fifteen days, or having left, has voluntarily returned. However, this period shall not include any period during which the person was unable to leave the territory of the Requesting Party for reasons beyond his or her control.

3. No penalty or coercive measure restricting personal liberty may be imposed on a person who refuses to testify or assist in an investigation under Article 10 or Article 11 by reason of such refusal.

Article 13 Search and Seizure

1. The Requested Party shall, to the extent permitted by its law, execute requests for the query, freezing, search, and seizure of property as evidence.

2. The Requested Party shall provide the Requesting Party with the results of the execution of such requests, including the results of the query or search, the location and condition of the frozen or seized property, and the subsequent custody of such property.

3. If the Requesting Party accepts the conditions imposed by the Requested Party regarding the transfer of seized property, the Requested Party may transfer the seized property to the Requesting Party.

Article 14 Return of Documents, Records, and Evidentiary Articles to the Requested Party

The Requesting Party shall return original documents, records, and evidentiary articles provided to it under this Treaty to the Requested Party as soon as possible upon request by the Requested Party, or when the Requesting Party no longer needs them.

Article 15 Confiscation of Proceeds and Instrumentalities of Crime

1. The Requested Party shall, upon request, endeavor to determine whether proceeds of crime or instrumentalities of crime are located in its territory and shall inform the Requesting Party of the results of its investigation. When making such request, the Requesting Party shall inform the Requested Party of the grounds for its belief that such property may be located in the territory of the Requested Party.

2. If, pursuant to paragraph 1 of this Article, suspected proceeds of crime or instrumentalities of crime are found, the Requested Party shall, upon request, take measures to freeze, seize, and confiscate such property in accordance with its law.

3. To the extent permitted by its law and under conditions agreed upon by the Parties, the Requested Party may, upon request by the Requesting Party, transfer all or part of the proceeds of crime or instrumentalities of crime, or the proceeds of the sale of such assets, to the Requesting Party.

Article 16 Notification of Results of Criminal Proceedings

The Requesting Party shall, upon request, notify the Requested Party of the results of the criminal proceedings to which a request made under this Treaty relates.

Article 17 Criminal Records

Upon request, the Requested Party shall provide the Requesting Party with information regarding previous criminal records and convictions of persons under investigation or prosecution in the Requesting Party, if such information is available in the territory of the Requested Party.

Article 18 Exchange of Legal Information

The Parties shall, upon request, exchange information on the law and judicial practice of their respective countries relevant to the implementation of this Treaty.

Article 19 Certification and Authentication of Documents

For the purposes of this Treaty, documents transmitted under this Treaty shall not require any form of certification or authentication, except as otherwise provided in this Treaty.

Article 20 Costs

1. The Requested Party shall bear the costs incurred in the execution of the request, except that the Requesting Party shall bear the following costs:

(a) the necessary and reasonable expenses of persons traveling to, staying in, and leaving the Requested Party pursuant to Article 8, paragraph 4;

(b) the necessary and reasonable expenses and allowances of persons traveling to, staying in, and leaving the Requesting Party pursuant to Article 10 or Article 11, which expenses and allowances shall be paid in accordance with the standards and regulations of the place where they are incurred;

(c) the necessary and reasonable expenses and fees of experts;

(d) the costs and fees of translation and interpretation.

2. The Requesting Party shall, upon request, advance the allowances, expenses, and fees it is required to bear.

3. If the execution of a request requires costs of an extraordinary nature, the Parties shall consult to determine the conditions under which the request may be executed.

Article 21 Service of Documents and Obtaining Evidence by Diplomatic or Consular Officers

A Party may serve documents and obtain evidence from its own nationals in the territory of the other Party through its diplomatic or consular officers stationed in the other Party, provided that this does not violate the law of the other Party and that no coercive measures are taken.

Article 22 Other Bases for Cooperation

This Treaty shall not preclude any Party from providing assistance to the other Party under other applicable international agreements or its domestic law. The Parties may also provide assistance under any other applicable arrangements, agreements, or practices.

Article 23 Consultation

The Parties shall, upon request by the other Party, consult promptly through their central authorities or diplomatic channels regarding the interpretation, application, or implementation of this Treaty, whether of a general nature or in relation to a specific case.

Article 24 Entry into Force, Amendment, and Termination

1. This Treaty is subject to ratification, and the instruments of ratification shall be exchanged in Manila. The Treaty shall enter into force on the thirtieth day after the exchange of instruments of ratification.

2. This Treaty may be amended at any time by written agreement between the Parties.

3. Either Party may terminate this Treaty at any time by giving written notice to the other Party through diplomatic channels. Termination shall take effect on the one hundred and eightieth day after the date of such notice.

4. This Treaty shall apply to requests made after its entry into force, even if the relevant acts or omissions occurred prior to the entry into force of this Treaty.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the undersigned, being duly authorized by their respective Governments, have signed this Treaty.

Done in duplicate at Beijing on October 16, 2000, in the Chinese and English languages, both texts being equally authentic.

For the People's Republic of China: Gao Changli (Signature)

For the Republic of the Philippines: Tu Kuilo (Signature)
